rounds.text: Lumax Auto Technologies Ltd is fundamentally under-appreciated because its impressive compounding and top-tier financial performance significantly outpace sector benchmarks. Compounded sales growth over 3 years reaches 38% [E16], while compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months surges by 77% [E21], vastly outperforming the sector median profit growth of 17.5% [E73]. This operational excellence translates into elite capital efficiency, demonstrated by a return on equity of 23.04% compared to a sector benchmark of 11.39% [E9], alongside a high rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 [E64]. Furthermore, the business is backed by a robust order book of INR 1,600 crore [E88], providing clear multi-year revenue visibility, including 24% execution slated for FY 27 and 56% for FY 28 [E89]. Conceded: the stock trades at a rich valuation with a price-to-earnings multiple of 37.7x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 10.30x [E2]. Yet, a reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies an earnings growth rate of only 15.0%, which is lower than the 18.0% base case assumption [E47], suggesting the market is still underestimating the firm's growth trajectory.

Lumax Auto Technologies Ltd carries a demanding valuation that outpaces standard benchmarks, with a P/E ratio of 37.7x and a price-to-book ratio of 10.30x compared to a sector P/B of 2.56x [E1, E2, E7]. This premium pricing leaves little room for error, as noted by the valuation blind-spot check which warns that the current price already discounts much of the good news [E70]. The financial structure also introduces visible leverage risks, with total borrowings expanding to ₹ 1,231 Cr in March 2026 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.02x where debt exceeds net worth [E37, E39]. Furthermore, institutional participation shows notable friction, marked by a sharp decline in foreign institutional holdings from 15.89% in December 2023 down to 8.89% in September 2026 [E42]. Historical price volatility is another underlying hazard, underscored by a severe past peak-to-trough drawdown of -85.2% and an annualized volatility reading of 47.6% [E53, E54]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing financial momentum, including a 10-year compounded profit growth of 25%, a 33% increase in TTM sales, and positive institutional money flow [E18, E19, E44, E65].

Yet, domestic institutions aggressively stepped in, surging from 8.32% to 17.12%, driving an overall positive institutional money flow (+0.78 percentage points) [E43, E44]. Nonetheless, the business generated substantial operating cash flow of ₹ 460 Cr and free cash flow of ₹ 214 Cr in March 2026, with profits fully backed by a cash conversion ratio of 1.36x [E34, E35, E36]. evidence.fact: A new facility will be set up in Nashik at Greenfuel Energy to cater to Mahindra's requirements.
evidence.quote: • At Greenfuel Energy, we are pleased to report that we onboarded Mahindra as a new customer and to cater to their requirements, we shall be setting up a new facility in Nashik.

evidence.quote: Only for few OEMs, maybe the spillover happens to the next quarter. But I would say to a great extent of 80% to 90%, we get the realization within the same quarter.

Mihir Ji, there was an amount of around INR 3-odd crore specifically for this particular Greenfuel division impacting around 3% on the EBITDA margins, which was one-off as a result of certain tooling revenue, which happened with the existing customer.
